clue.text: Meeting finding improbable treatment for software?

parts.note: an app is a piece of software, short for application
an ointment is a medical treatment, though an improbable one to rub on a computer program

explanation.surface: A meeting where someone hits on an odd remedy for buggy computer programs.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay pictures balm spread on an app: the software comes first, then the salve.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointment is an arranged engagement with someone at a set time, the same thing as a meeting.

clue.text: Narrated story of wolf blowing houses down? That's hairy!

indicators.note: something narrated is told out loud, so we want the spoken sound of the phrase, not its spelling

parts.words: story of wolf blowing houses down
parts.note: the wolf huffs and puffs at the houses in the fairy tale of the Three Little Pigs, a pig tale

explanation.surface: Someone retells the Big Bad Wolf story and remarks on how hair-raising it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's hairy!' reads as a comment on a scary story, but it defines a hairstyle: a plait of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigtail is a braid or bunch of hair hanging from the head, so it is literally a hairy thing.

clue.text: Unqualified, twice dismissed?

wordplay.note: a batter dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the wordplay reading: a player given out on two occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: Unqualified here means complete or absolute, as in an out-and-out lie, with no reservations attached.

clue.text: Dark near end of street

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: end of tells us to keep only the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the last letter of street

explanation.surface: A shadowy spot close to where a road runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark is a common noun for nighttime, the hours without daylight, as in afraid of the dark.

clue.text: Wine merchant briefly under doctor

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
in a down clue, under places the first piece beneath the second one in the column

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
a merchant is someone who sells

explanation.surface: A wine dealer who works only briefly beneath a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is a German white wine named after the river valley where its grapes are grown.

clue.text: A steeplechaser at the back, once more upended, falls

indicators.note: upended means turned upside down, which in a down entry flips the order of the letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at the back points to the rearmost letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of steeplechaser
once more means again

explanation.surface: A horse in a steeplechase, trailing at the back, tumbles again at a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like the horse falling over, but it is the noun: a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the border between Canada and the United States.

clue.text: Every diamond, for example, in area on ship?

wordplay.note: diamonds are one of four suits, so all of them together make up a quarter of a deck of cards

explanation.surface: A card player gathers all the diamonds, perhaps on a cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Every diamond' as the whole suit: thirteen cards of a fifty-two card pack.
explanation.definitionFit: The quarterdeck is the raised rear part of a ship's upper deck, traditionally reserved for officers.

clue.text: Return for match

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
to fit is to match or suit

explanation.surface: Asking what someone gets back in exchange for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A return on an investment is the gain made from it, which is exactly what profit means.

clue.text: Cheerful, just like some pianos

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in good spirits, as in feeling more upbeat
third meaning: a piano whose strings run vertically rather than horizontally like a grand

explanation.walkthrough: 'just like' reads as one phrase meaning similar to, but 'just' is a meaning of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright describes an honest, principled person, and also the vertical style of domestic piano as opposed to a grand.

clue.text: Chatterbox adoring senseless babbling, initially breaking silence

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into the middle of something, so these letters go inside

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them

indicators.note: initially tells us to keep only the opening letter of each word

parts.note: the first letters of adoring, senseless and babbling

explanation.surface: A talkative person whose doting nonsense shatters a quiet moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is an informal insult for someone who talks too much, just like a chatterbox.

clue.text: Big names born in Leicester, I gathered

indicators.note: gathered suggests bunched up and pleated, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: b is the standard abbreviation for born, as in biographies
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Famous people who were born in the English city of Leicester, I've learned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gathered' sounds like 'I understand', but gathered is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Big names is an idiom for famous people, the stars whom everyone recognises.

clue.text: Stop chorus

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to hold back from doing something
second meaning: a noun, the repeated lines of a song

explanation.surface: Someone yells at the singers to quit the chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to abstain or desist, and a refrain is the recurring part of a song between verses.

clue.text: Register years on earth, digging

parts.note: a till is a cash register
your age is the number of years you have been alive

explanation.surface: Recording how long someone has lived, while they dig in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the work of preparing soil by ploughing and turning it, which is a kind of digging.

clue.text: Ultimately invisible, brainbox went to school for praise

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so we take the closing letter of each following word

parts.note: the final letters of invisible, brainbox, went, to and school

explanation.surface: A clever pupil who went unnoticed at school, in the end earning praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly or enthusiastically, so the verb matches the verb.

clue.text: A rave gone mad, usually

indicators.note: gone mad suggests wild disorder, so the letters are jumbled up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; it doubles as part of the signal

explanation.surface: Dance parties typically get out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: On average is an idiom meaning typically or as a rule, so it stands in for usually.

clue.text: Comic operas, brilliant atmosphere

indicators.note: comic means funny and absurd, so the following letters are played around with

parts.note: taken as written
ace is slang for excellent or brilliant

explanation.surface: Funny operas with a wonderful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atmosphere' looks like mood, but it means the air around the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerospace is the earth's atmosphere together with outer space beyond it, the region aircraft and rockets travel.

clue.text: Interior designer, one delivering Christmas lecture?

parts.note: Christmas falls in December, abbreviated Dec
an orator is one who delivers speeches and lectures

explanation.surface: An interior designer who gives a festive talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsical split: a December orator, someone giving a talk at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator paints, papers and furnishes rooms, the job of someone who designs interiors.

clue.text: Chap oddly claiming a foul after cut in card game

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the outer letters wrap around what follows
oddly means keep only the letters in odd-numbered positions

parts.note: the first and third letters of chap
taken as written

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: foul means nasty

explanation.surface: A man oddly accusing someone of foul play after the cut in a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game for two or more players, using two packs of cards.

clue.text: Take position of agent on thread

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the second one in the column

parts.note: a rep, or representative, is a sales agent
a lace is a cord or thread, as in a shoelace

explanation.surface: Someone stepping into the spot of an agent who is busy sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace someone is to take over their role or stand in their stead.

clue.text: Seaside platform hosting piano player

indicators.note: hosting means having a guest inside, so one letter sits within the other word

parts.note: a pier is a platform built out over the sea at a resort
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A seaside pier that has a piano for the entertainers.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper is a musician who plays the pipes or bagpipes, so a player of an instrument.

clue.text: Word in mantra brought into force

indicators.note: brought into means placed inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: to prise something open is to force it
om is the sacred syllable chanted as a mantra

explanation.surface: A word from a chant that is enacted and given force.
explanation.walkthrough: Prise is the British spelling of prize, meaning to lever open.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving your word means making a pledge, so word is a synonym for a solemn undertaking.

clue.text: Supporter in thrall I picked up

indicators.note: picked up in a down entry means lifted from bottom to top, so read backwards
in means the letters lie inside the following words, crossing their gaps

parts.note: a run of letters straddling thrall, I and picked

explanation.surface: A fan, enthralled, says they were chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' tempts as gathered, but only up does the work; picked supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is a column that holds up a structure, a supporter in the literal sense.

clue.text: Snacks primate found in tins

indicators.note: found in means discovered inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: cans are tins
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Nibbles, with a monkey discovered among the tinned goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Canapes are small savoury bites served at parties, a kind of snack.

clue.text: Separate city in Croatia

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to divide or break apart
second meaning: the port on the Dalmatian coast

explanation.surface: A Croatian city standing apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To split is to divide into parts, and Split is Croatia's second-largest city, on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Container seen through opening, illuminated

indicators.note: seen through suggests glimpsed within a gap, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a slit is a narrow opening
a pot is a container

explanation.surface: A jar glimpsed through a gap, caught in the light.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotlit means lit up by a spotlight, a particular way of being illuminated.

clue.text: Attack a small boat

parts.note: taken as written
s is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
sail can mean a sailing vessel, a boat

explanation.surface: An order to raid a little vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently or vigorously, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Breathe life into a friend touring Northern Ireland

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the outer letters surround the inner ones

parts.note: a, plus mate meaning friend
NI is the standard abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Livening up a pal who is on a trip around Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to give life or vitality to something, a verb matching the verb phrase.

clue.text: Items here collected by mum and dad, afterthoughts

indicators.note: collected by means picked up and held, so one piece is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: parens is an informal word for parents
these refers to items here, as opposed to those over there

explanation.surface: Things that parents gathered up, as if remembered at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: Parens is also an abbreviation for parentheses, a neat echo in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Parentheses are brackets enclosing extra remarks, the asides added as afterthoughts in a sentence.
